messages:
Mia: Heads-up — over the past 36h we've seen repeated GPU node flapping in us-west2 (nodes cycling NotReady then back). These produce a bunch of low-severity alerts that currently page on duty. Thinking we should tighten when we page vs create a ticket so oncall is not paged for short blips. Thoughts?

Ahmed: +1, saw the same. Most spikes are 1-2m and then recover. Paging for each one is noisy. Do we have a reliable metric to distinguish transient vs real incidents?

Mia: Prometheus has node_condition{condition="Ready", job="kube-state-metrics"} and we also get node_boot_time and pod_eviction_count per node. Proposal: only page if node is NotReady for >5m OR if we see >3 nodes in the same AZ flapping within 10m. Otherwise create a ticket and aggregate in the SRE queue.

Liz: That seems reasonable. Suggest adding a hysteresis so a quick flip doesn't re-open the page: alert should require sustained state for X samples (e.g., 3 samples @ 1m scrape). Also group by region+rack label so we don't page for a single tenant's scheduled maintenance.

Sam: Also add a runbook link in the alert and an automatic ticket creation for non-paging alerts. We already have a ticket webhook. For paging alerts, include context: recent deployments, GPU driver restarts, and node age.

Ahmed: Example PromQL for the sustained condition: 
```
avg_over_time((kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready",status="false"} == 1)[5m:1m]) > 0
```
That gives us nodes that have been false for most of the last 5m. For the multi-node grouping: 
```
count by (zone) (avg_over_time((kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready",status="false"} == 1)[5m:1m]) > 0) > 2
```

Kevin: Couple of policy suggestions: 
- Page severity: P1 for >25% of cluster nodes down in a region or >3 AZs affected. 
- P2 (page after acknowledgement window) for >3 nodes in one AZ sustained >10m. 
- P3: ticket only for single node flaps shorter than 10m.

Mia: Also propose quiet window for non-prod clusters 23:00-06:00 PST where single-node flaps create tickets only. For prod we keep paging rules but with thresholds above.

Liz: We should add a mute-suppression rule for ongoing maintenance. Maybe use a `maintenance=true` node label or prow job annotations to automatically silence.

Sam: I'll draft the alert rule changes. Action items: Sam to open PR with new Prometheus rules and grouping labels, Ahmed to add the PromQL examples and unit tests, Mia to update the runbook and ticket templates. Kevin to sign off on severity thresholds.

OncallBot: Created issue #INF-7345 in infra/ops: "Alert tuning: gpu node flap paging vs ticketing (us-west2)" (priority: P3).

Ahmed: Quick question — what about cache/kv workload latency impact during flaps? Should we include application-level error-rate correlation in the paging criteria?

Mia: Good call. Add a correlate check: if RPC error-rate or tail latency on critical services spikes >2x concurrently with node flaps, escalate to paging immediately. Otherwise ticket. I'll add the list of services in the runbook.

Kevin: Sounds good. Once PR is up we'll run the rules in the staging prometheus for 24h and review false-positive counts, then ship to prod. :thumbsup:

Sam: PR in review: https://git.internal/redwood/prometheus/compare/alert-tuning-gpu-flap — includes `for` durations, grouping by `region,zone`, runbook links, and ticket webhook.

Liz: Thanks — if testing shows <2 false pages/day we'll merge. If not, iterate on the `for` window and grouping label set.

Mia: Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate the rollout schedule and ping infra calendar.

Kevin: Appreciate the pragmatic thresholds.
